item.title: Barcelona making it hard for Arsenal to sign Premier League sensation
item.description: Barcelona making it hard for Arsenal to sign Premier League sensation Eli Junior Kroupi has been one of the top strikers in the Premier League and was the best-scoring teenager in the competition last season. At the end of that term, Arsenal wanted to sign him , but he opted to remain at Bournemouth and then suffered a serious injury that still keeps him out of action for Bournemouth. He is still not back, but Arsenal continues to keep an eye on him as a player to sign and improve their team when the season ends. The Gunners may have to make that happen in January because they have serious competition, and Fichajes says Barcelona wants to sign the Frenchman. Arsenal’s Interest in Kroupi Barcelona see him as one of the top young strikers on the continent and would love to add him to their squad, as they have given up on signing Julian Alvarez. Arsenal wants Alvarez too, but it will be easier for them to sign Kroupi, so they will do their best to beat Barca to sign him, which will be tough. The Frenchman’s talent is not in question, and his goal-scoring record speaks for itself, but the competition for his signature is fierce. Arsenal’s interest is genuine, but they are not the only club monitoring the situation. The Battle for His Signature The report says the Catalans will do all their best to add him to their squad and make him an important member of their team in the coming transfer window. Barca signed Gabriel Jesus in the summer , but he is not who they truly wanted, and Kroupi could bench him in Catalonia. The striker’s injury is a concern, but his potential is enormous, and the big clubs are circling. Arsenal’s need for a striker is clear, and Kroupi fits the profile. The fans will be hoping the club can get the deal done. The coming weeks will show whether Arsenal can beat Barcelona to his signature, as the race heats up. Kroupi’s future is uncertain, but a move to a bigger club seems likely. item.title: FIFA launches investigation after racism allegation as England walk out of U15 World Cup game
item.description: England's Under-15 FIFA World Cup game against the Republic of Ireland was abandoned after an alleged racist incident, after which the Three Lions walked off -Credit:Reach Publishing Services Limited FIFA are investigating an allegation of racist abuse by a Republic of Ireland player that resulted in the abandonment of England's Under-15 World Cup match. The incident occurred during Monday's fixture in Azerbaijan, when an England player was observed approaching the touchline to alert his coaching staff of the alleged abuse, before the complaint was brought to the official's attention. England's coaching staff subsequently instructed their players to exit the pitch, with the Republic of Ireland holding a 4-1 advantage entering the final minute of the game. FIFA have since confirmed they are examining the incident and collecting reports to determine the circumstances surrounding the allegation. "Fifa is aware of an incident at the U-15 World Cup and Festival match between England and the Republic of Ireland," a spokesperson said, via The Mirror . "The match was abandoned by the referee following England's refusal to continue. Cristiano Ronaldo delivers brutal Portugal 'ultimatum' after Jorge Jesus 'broke his word' Erik ten Hag 'embarrassed' by Scott McTominay transfer as ex-Man United manager slams club bosses -Credit:Robert Hradil, Getty Images "The official reports are being gathered, and the matter will be referred to the independent disciplinary committee, who will decide in due course." England head coach Matt Thorpe was observed summoning the referee over before directing his players to leave the field. Thorpe was reportedly informed by the official that he 'could not hear.' One of Thorpe's assistant coaches was then heard informing the official, 'We are reporting racism,' before stating, 'We do not want to play.' It was later reported that a player was 'upset.' A tense confrontation reportedly occurred between the two coaching staffs as both teams attempted to safeguard their players. Neither the FA nor the FAI have issued a statement concerning the incident at this time.

item.description: Ulster boss Richie Murphy is without his nine-strong Ireland cohort in Cape Town [Getty Images] On the face of it, Ulster are without a victory in their four United Rugby Championship outings this season. But head coach Richie Murphy is not ready to hit the panic button. Despite a winless start, the Irish province are just one point outside the play-off places despite a struggle for results. An opening defeat by Edinburgh was followed by two thrilling draws against Glasgow and Munster, and then a loss to the Bulls in the first of a South African double-header. There has been a constant theme throughout: Ulster have allowed the opposition to build an early - and often significant - lead. On each occasion they have fought back, but have yet to seal a comeback with victory. Murphy admits his side have been "digging a bit of a hole" in each of their four matches this season. "Obviously, we're not quite getting the results that we wanted, but we're in every game," said Murphy, whose side defeated Zebre in their Challenge Cup opener. "We're playing against top-class opposition and we're fighting for everything we can get." "It's really important that we don't throw the baby out with the bathwater. We will stick to our process and stick to what we believe in, and that's what we're trying to do." McNabney keen to show Ireland coaches 'what I'm all about' Murphy praises Ulster for 'sticking in the fight' 'We strive for consistency' Despite admitting the opening results have left him with "mixed emotions", Murphy feels his side "can compete with the best teams in the league". "We're not a million miles away from winning opportunities to win every one of those matches," he added. "We're just trying to double down on the areas that we need to improve. But head coach Richie Murphy is not ready to hit the panic button. Despite a winless start, the Irish province are just one point outside the play-off places despite a struggle for results. An opening defeat by Edinburgh was followed by two thrilling draws against Glasgow and Munster, and then a loss to the Bulls in the first of a South African double-header. There has been a constant theme throughout: Ulster have allowed the opposition to build an early - and often significant - lead. On each occasion they have fought back, but have yet to seal a comeback with victory. Murphy admits his side have been "digging a bit of a hole" in each of their four matches this season. "Obviously, we're not quite getting the results that we wanted, but we're in every game," said Murphy, whose side defeated Zebre in their Challenge Cup opener. "We're playing against top-class opposition and we're fighting for everything we can get." "It's really important that we don't throw the baby out with the bathwater. We will stick to our process and stick to what we believe in, and that's what we're trying to do." McNabney keen to show Ireland coaches 'what I'm all about' Murphy praises Ulster for 'sticking in the fight' 'We strive for consistency' Despite admitting the opening results have left him with "mixed emotions", Murphy feels his side "can compete with the best teams in the league". "We're not a million miles away from winning opportunities to win every one of those matches," he added. "We're just trying to double down on the areas that we need to improve. If you ask me what areas are they, it's a little bit of everything. "If we could be a little bit better at the breakdown, or if our pass quality could be a little bit better. All these tiny little aspects of the game add up to wins." If Ulster are to pick up an elusive first URC victory of the season, Murphy knows that consistency is going to be key - starting against the Stormers in Cape Town on Saturday (12:45 GMT). "In each of the games that we've played, we've played some very high-class rugby in both attack and defence, but we haven't been consistent," he said. "The thing that we strive for is consistency and if our execution can very slightly improve, it's amazing what that will do to the results. "We'll stick to the process, believe in what we're trying to do and we believe that the results will come." 'A different headache' While Ulster have been soaking up the heat in South Africa - a stark contrast to the current weather back home - Murphy knows his side are about to face a storm of a different kind on Saturday. The Stormers will likely have their Springbok stars available - such as Siya Kolisi, back row Evan Roos and fly-half Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu - which is not a luxury Murphy will have. In fact, Ulster head to Cape Town without nine of their key players after they were called up for Ireland duty ahead of November's Nations Championship fixtures. Backs Stuart McCloskey, Jacob Stockdale, Robert Baloucoune, Nathan Doak and Jamie Benson have been included along with forwards Tom O'Toole, Tom Stewart, James McNabney and Nick Timoney. The experience of hooker Rob Herring and centre James Hume should help to fill the void despite their lack of minutes through injury, and returning wing Zac Ward will offer plenty of try-scoring prowess. Murphy admits it "causes a different headache for us" having so many players unavailable. "We didn't know the amount of players we were going to lose and nine is probably more than we were expecting. "But at the same time, we're delighted for those players to get the opportunity to go and represent Ireland." James McNabney (left) and Jamie Benson (with the ball) have been called into Andy Farrell's Ireland squad [Getty Images] Of the nine players called up for Ireland's Nations Championship games in November, Benson and McNabney have been called up for the first time. Murphy said Benson, a versatile Irish-qualified former England Under-20 international, has been "excellent" since joining from Harlequins in the summer. The 24-year-old has featured in both centre positions and fly-half for Ulster, and can also play at full-back. "He has shown good signs of leadership in our group as well and his attitude has been so good in relation to playing in three different positions "That versatility is really good for any squad and Ireland are obviously recognising that as well." Back row McNabney, who Farrell described as "some specimen", has been included after recovering from a year on the sidelines with an ACL injury. "He's finding his feet in a little bit, but you can see the attributes that he has," said Murphy. "It's great to have those guys in there, but it obviously puts pressure on our squad."

item.title: Is the NASCAR Championship Out of Reach for Ryan Blaney After Talladega?
item.description: Photo by: Gary A. Vasquez Ryan Blaney’s hopes of winning another NASCAR Cup Series championship have taken a serious hit following Sunday’s chaotic race at Talladega Superspeedway. After being collected in a major accident, the Team Penske driver finds himself facing a difficult challenge with only two races remaining in the 2026 season. Blaney entered Talladega hoping to gain ground in the championship standings, but his afternoon ended prematurely after a multicar accident on Lap 133. The crash also involved several other Chase contenders, including Tyler Reddick, Chase Elliott and Denny Hamlin. Blaney was unable to continue and finished 38th, leaving him with significant ground to make up heading into the final two races. Talladega Creates Major Championship Problems The biggest problem for Blaney is the points deficit he now faces. Following the Talladega race, Blaney sits sixth in the championship standings, 107 points behind leader Kyle Larson. Larson delivered a remarkable performance, winning the race after charging through the field on the final lap. The victory gave him a commanding advantage and dramatically changed the championship picture. With only two races remaining, Blaney needs nearly everything to go his way. He must deliver strong finishes while hoping Larson encounters trouble or loses significant points. The 38th-place finish was especially costly because Blaney had been in position to challenge for the championship before the accident. Instead, he leaves Talladega with a much steeper climb. Blaney acknowledged his role in the incident, explaining that the aggressive racing and three-wide positioning contributed to the crash. While the accident was frustrating, the immediate priority was making sure everyone involved was safe. Can Blaney Still Make a Comeback? Despite the setback, Blaney cannot be ruled out entirely. The upcoming race at Martinsville Speedway could provide an opportunity to recover valuable points. Blaney has enjoyed success at Martinsville, including victories in two of the previous three fall races entering this season. That history provides some reason for optimism heading into the next event. However, the challenge remains enormous. Larson has built a substantial advantage, and Blaney has very little room for another disappointing result. The championship is not mathematically out of reach, but Blaney’s chances are fading quickly. He will need a near-perfect finish to the season and significant help from Larson’s results to keep his title hopes alive. After Talladega, Blaney’s championship pursuit is on life support. Martinsville may represent his best remaining opportunity to change the story.

item.title: No QB controversy: Kubiak backs Kirk Cousins as starter
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders QB Kirk Cousins (8) dives for a first down in the first quarter of a game against the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada. Standing at a crossroads in their 2026 season, the Las Vegas Raiders are beginning to hear the conversations surrounding their future. After suffering their fourth straight loss at the hands of the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was open to making any changes necessary to turn the season around. “I think, at this point, we’re thinking about everything,” admitted Kubiak at Sunday’s postgame press conference. Some of the immediate post-game discourse included whether or not Fernando Mendoza would get starts at quarterback in place of Kirk Cousins, and the signs have been there to justify such theories. In the blowout loss to the New England Patriots in Week Five, Mendoza played the final series of the game and looked solid, completing six of his eight passes for 48 yards. There was also a sequence against the Rams where it looked like Mendoza was warming up to take over, but it turned out to be a false alarm as Cousins finished out the game. However, Kubiak started his Monday press conference early by backing Cousins, indicating that he will be the starting quarterback against the New York Jets on Sunday. “Kirk is our starting quarterback. There is no controversy there,” Kubiak stated. “He is playing at a very high level, and we got to continue to do that in order to win.” In fairness, the quarterback position is pretty far down the list of the issues plaguing the Raiders right now. Cousins may have struggled in the first half against the Rams, but he has been largely solid outside of that. In seven games, Cousins has thrown for 1,877 yards and an NFL-leading 16 touchdowns. item.description: MLB insider reveals Yankees' 'most realistic' free agent target at catcher originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees desperately need a right-handed hitting catcher. Ali Sanchez was the primary backup behind Austin Wells, but he offers little upside on offense. The Yankees could keep Sanchez as catching depth, but they would be better off finding a veteran with better offensive numbers. The Athletic's Chris Kirschner wrote that New York's front office should be looking for a new catcher and it's a "must" for this winter. He tabbed an 11-year veteran who spent the last two years with the Chicago Cubs as the top candidate. "The Yankees have options to consider in free agency. Carson Kelly might be the best and most realistic option available," Kirschner wrote. "He's expected to decline his $7.5 million mutual option with the Chicago Cubs and become a free agent. Kelly posted a 143 wRC+ against left-handed pitching this season and has 123 wRC+ against lefties in his career," Kirschner added. "He also grades out well in blocks above average, according to Statcast, and is slightly above average in framing, a key metric the Yankees focus on when considering catchers." MORE : Dodgers facing tricky question over Shohei Ohtani's future as a two-way player Kirschner adds that Wells had a 19 wRC+ against left-handed pitching in 2026, so adding a right-handed platoon partner is necessary. At the very least, the Yankees would feel confident that Kelly can provide above-average production against southpaws. Other free agent backstops the Yankees could consider are Ryan Jeffers, Tyler Stephenson, Austin Hedges, or a reunion with Gary Sanchez or Kyle Higashioka. item.title: Here is what coach Jeff Hafley had to say after Dolphins' first win
item.description: MIAMI GARDENS — The Miami Dolphins enter the week for the first time in 2026 coming off a win. After the 28-25 victory at the New York Jets, the Dolphins now seek their first win at home in 2026 and get that chance Sunday when they host the New England Patriots . Coach Jeff Hafley kicked off the week meeting with the media to talk about the first victory of the season for the Dolphins (1-5) and the first victory of his NFL head-coaching career. item.title: Is the NASCAR Championship Out of Reach for Denny Hamlin After Talladega?
item.description: Photo by: Scott Kinser Denny Hamlin’s hopes of finally capturing his first NASCAR Cup Series championship took another major hit Sunday at Talladega Superspeedway. Despite finishing eighth in the YellaWood 500, Hamlin finds himself in a difficult position with just two races remaining in the 2026 season. Kyle Larson’s dramatic victory changed the championship picture, giving the defending champion a commanding 73-point lead over Hamlin. With the season rapidly approaching its conclusion, the question now becomes whether the Joe Gibbs Racing driver can pull off one final comeback. Hamlin Faces an Uphill Battle Hamlin entered the 2026 Chase as the No. 1 seed after putting together an impressive regular season. The veteran driver collected four victories and established himself as one of the strongest championship contenders. However, the postseason has been a different story. While Hamlin has managed to remain near the top of the standings, mistakes, mechanical issues and unfortunate circumstances have prevented him from consistently challenging for victories. Talladega offered another example. Hamlin survived a major accident and managed to keep his No. 11 Toyota competitive despite sustaining damage. He was even in contention during the closing laps before contact disrupted his momentum, leaving him with an eighth-place finish. Meanwhile, Larson capitalized on the chaos to secure the victory and extend his advantage. Can Hamlin Still Win the Championship? Although Hamlin’s championship hopes have taken a significant hit, he has not been mathematically eliminated. With two races remaining, there are still opportunities to gain ground. Martinsville Speedway presents an especially important opportunity for Hamlin, who has historically performed well at the Virginia short track. However, the challenge is enormous. Hamlin needs strong finishes while hoping Larson encounters trouble or fails to collect enough points to maintain his advantage. The pressure will be on Hamlin and the entire Joe Gibbs Racing organization to deliver when it matters most. Another Heartbreaking Ending? Hamlin has spent years chasing the one accomplishment missing from his Hall of Fame-caliber career. His four victories this season demonstrate that he still has the speed to compete for a championship. Unfortunately, speed alone might not be enough. The championship is not officially out of reach, but Hamlin’s chances are quickly fading. Unless he produces a major performance at Martinsville and Larson finally stumbles, 2026 could become another painful chapter in Hamlin’s pursuit of his first Cup Series title.

item.title: Where is former WTA World No. 8 Anna Kournikova?
item.description: Long before Sophie Cunningham, the female athlete “it girl” was WTA tennis star Anna Kournikova, 45. Kournikova’s career spanned from 1995-2003, when social media was not a thing. Yet she was among the internet’s most searched athletes for years after her playing career ended prematurely because of injuries. Kournikova’s on-court success was mainly in doubles where she reached the World No. 1 ranking. She partnered with Martina Hingis to win two Grand Slams and two WTA finals titles. They nicknamed themselves the “Spice Girls of tennis.” Her career high singles ranking was World No. 8. She had a drink and computer virus named after her. The Anna Kournikova cocktail was a white Russian made with skim milk. In 2001, the Anna Kournikova computer virus wreaked havoc. MORE: Where is former WTA World No. 1 Maria Sharapova? Kournikova is the mother of three children to Enrique Iglesias Nov. 15, 2010; Washington, D.C, USA; Anna Kournikova at the WTT Smash Hits at American University. They live in Miami with their three children, fraternal twins Lucy and Nicholas and another daughter named Mary. A Russian by birth, Kournikova competed for Russia while playing, but she became an American citizen after she retired. Because of the scrutiny surrounding Kournikova in her formative years, she is fiercely protective and private of her children. She was the victim of a 2005 stalker incident where the person intended to swim to her house but went to the wrong address. item.title: Eagles announce five additions to 53-man roster before MNF vs. Cowboys
item.description: Eagles announce five additions to 53-man roster before MNF vs. Cowboys originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . With Jalen Hurts out for the rest of the 2026 NFL season, the Philadelphia Eagles will be rolling with Tanner McKee as the starting quarterback going forward. While the Eagles have dealt with plenty of injury issues this season, heading into Monday Night Football against the Dallas Cowboys , they got some good news about a few key offensive players coming off injured reserve. Prior to Monday Night Football against the rival Cowboys, the Eagles announced that five players were added to the roster for this matchup, including second-round rookie tight end Eli Stowers for his NFL debut. Eagles add five players to 53-man roster for MNF vs. Cowboys "We have activated TE Grant Calcaterra, G Landon Dickerson, and TE Eli Stowers from Injured Reserve," the Eagles announced. "We have also elevated OLB Keyshawn James-Newby and RB Elijah Mitchell for tonight's game. CB Jakorian Bennett (knee)) has been ruled out for the game." Bennett will remain on IR for the Eagles for one more week, but they got some great news with Calcaterra, Dickerson, and Stowers' return to the 53-man roster. Dickerson can take back over at left guard for the Eagles, giving them three-fifths of their Week 1 offensive line back, with only Lane Johnson's retirement and Cam Jurgens' trade making up the holes on the OL. James-Newby is much-needed edge rusher depth, and Mitchell might see some work in MNF with Saquon Barkley not yet 100%, and Dameon Pierce not overly impressing this season for Philadelphia. MORE : NFL insiders reveal four landing spots for Colts ’ Jonathan Taylor But the most exciting player joining the roster with these roster moves is obviously second-round rookie tight end Eli Stowers. While he's not shown a whole lot yet, he hasn't even had a chance to play in the NFL. Hurts won't be the one throwing him the ball, but McKee, who he likely had plenty of reps with during the preseason and training camp, will be. Stowers and Makai Lemon might need to have a big day against Dallas, as DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are out, leaving Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Stowers, and Dallas Goedert as the top pass-catching options. This is a big game for the Eagles, as a loss could have Philly considering a trade deadline sell-off, while a win could potentially convince the Eagles they can contend for the NFC East title this season. Stroud, who guided the Texans downfield for a 3-yard touchdown pass to Xaiver Hutchinson with less than a minute left, had two touchdown passes but finished with a season-low 153 passing yards. The run game once again was limited, as Houston rushed for 84 yards on 26 carries between Dare Ogunbowale and Woody Marks. Perhaps the big win of the afternoon came with the return of wide receiver Tank Dell. After suffering a knee injury in December 2024, Dell spent nearly two years recovering from the injury. Stewart to see the bulk of the snaps at safety with Reed Blankenship out. He played on 94% of snaps and recorded a team-tying 11 tackles. item.title: Badgers star earns Big Ten Player of the Week award after stellar performance
item.description: IOWA CITY, IA - OCTOBER 24: Running back King Miller #8 of the USC Trojans goes up the field in the first half against linebacker Sebastian Cheeks #15 of the Wisconsin Badgers at Camp Randall Stadium on October 24, 2026 in Madison, WI. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time since November of last year, the Wisconsin Badgers have a Big Ten Defensive Player of the Week. After a six-pressure, 2.5-sack performance, Sebastian Cheeks was named the Big Ten Defensive Player of the Week, marking the first time a Badger has won the award since Darryl Peterson against the Illinois Fighting Illini last year. Cheeks, who has been one of the best edge rushers in the country this year, wreaked havoc on the quarterback while also recording four defensive stops. He had six pressures and a 17.1 percent pass rush win rate, according to PFF. That puts him at 34 pressures for the year, and it was a nice bounce-back after he had just one pressure against UCLA, due to the constant chipping and double teams. Here’s what the Big Ten said about Cheeks in its announcement: Posted five tackles and 2.5 sacks in Wisconsin’s win against No. 16 USC at Camp Randall on Saturday night His five tackles included the three parts of sacks and two stops for no gain Helped the Badgers hold USC to -17 yards rushing, which ranks as the second-best mark in Wisconsin school history and the best by a defense in Division I college football this season Last Wisconsin Defensive Player of the Week honoree: Darryl Peterson (Nov. 24, 2025) Elsewhere, Northwestern’s Aidan Chiles won Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week after accounting for over 300 yards and five touchdowns in a blowout win over Rutgers. Minnesota’s Luke Drzewiecki won the Big Ten Special Teams Player of the Week honor, while Illinois’s Michael Clayton was the Big Ten Freshman of the Week. Cheeks has been the star of an elite Badgers defense, as he has 34 pressures and 18 defensive stops in seven games for Wisconsin, which is more than he had all of last season. According to PFF, he is second among Power 4 edge rushers in pressures this season, with only Virginia’s Matthew Fobbs-White (35 pressures) having more, although the latter has played in one more game than Cheeks this season.

Tottenham and Nottingham Forest are both understood to have scouted him, while Napoli, FC Porto and Borussia Dortmund are also tracking developments. There is already evidence of serious interest. item.title: Emegha To Lead The Line | 3-4-2-1 Chelsea Predicted Lineup Vs Liverpool
item.description: Emegha To Lead The Line | 3-4-2-1 Chelsea Predicted Lineup Vs Liverpool Chelsea will lock horns with Liverpool at Anfield this Wednesday night as they look to secure a good result away from home in the EFL Cup. The Blues suffered a lackluster 2-0 loss at the hands of Tottenham Hotspur in the London derby recently, so they would be eager to put in a much-improved showing in midweek. Xabi Alonso will set his men up in a 3-4-2-1 formation and is expected to make a lot of changes to his first team for this game. Emmanuel Emegha could get the nod to lead the line for the West London club up top if he can recover in time for this game. 3-4-2-1 Chelsea Predicted Lineup To Face Liverpool Defence Mike Penders will operate in goal for Chelsea after conceding two goals in his last appearance. Alonso could name a back three of Wesley Fofana, Maxence Lacroix and Josh Acheampong for this game as they look to keep the opposition at bay during the 90 minutes. Levi Colwill will offer cover for the centre-back positions on the bench. LONDON, ENGLAND – OCTOBER 24: Mike Penders of Chelsea reacts during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Chelsea FC and Tottenham Hotspur at Stamford Bridge on October 24, 2026 in London, England. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) Midfield Valentin Barco and Romeo Lavia will anchor the midfield for the Blues as they look to make life difficult for the home team in the middle of the park. Malo Gusto will try to impress as the right-sided wide player, while Marco Palestra looks to give a good account of himself on the left flank. Both of them will be expected to make some overlapping runs out in the wide areas. Danny Welbeck and Estevao will assume the duties of Alonso’s attacking midfielders. Both of them need to combine well if the Blues are to stand a chance of earning a win at Anfield in midweek. Moises Caicedo and Pedro Neto will be rested on the bench and might come on to influence the game in the second half if required. Attack Emmanuel Emegha is a major doubt for this game, but could get a chance to impress from the start of this clash if he can pass a late fitness test. Morgan Rogers will get a rest on the bench as he waits for his chance to shine in the latter stages of the game if the Blues are in need of a goal by then.

item.title: Ballon d’Or chaos as Harry Kane, Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe published as winners on website
item.description: The Ballon d’Or has been plunged into chaos after its official website published three separate articles claiming Harry Kane , Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe had all won the prestigious individual award before the start of the ceremony . The world’s best player of 2026 will be crowned tonight at the London Palladium with Bayern Munich and England striker Kane the favourite , off the back of 89 goals for club and country in just 81 appearances since the start of last season. Follow the Ballon d’Or 2026 LIVE! But in a seemingly colossal error by organisers, Kane was one of three winners promoted by the award’s official website at approximately 5:15pm GMT, hours before proceedings got underway, with Barcelona sensation Yamal and Real Madrid striker Mbappe - the two other frontrunners - getting similar articles posted. The articles were then down by the website at around 5:45pm GMT. Harry Kane was one of three to be claimed the Ballon d'Or winner in articles published before the ceremony (Ballon d'Or) Kane’s article was headlined: “Harry Kane wins 2026 Ballon d’Or: Here are his best and most meaningful strikes from a 61-goal season”, which went on to examine his “prolific haul” and records that “ensured Bayern won a domestic treble”. item.title: New England Revolution legend Andrew Farrell announces retirement
item.description: New England Revolution legend Andrew Farrell announces retirement By MLSsoccer staff New England Revolution defender Andrew Farrell has announced his retirement from professional soccer following the 2026 season, concluding a 14-year career spent entirely with the club. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2013 MLS SuperDraft out of the University of Louisville, Farrell holds New England's all-time records for games played (389), games started (352) and minutes played (33k+). "This club has meant everything to me," an emotional Farrell said in his retirement announcement . "For as long as I've known, it's what I've always wanted to do, and so that ending is always tough. But I loved every minute of it, and just grateful for the opportunity to be part of the club and this community." Farrell helped New England reach MLS Cup in 2014 and win the Supporters' Shield in 2021, when the Revolution set a then-league record with 73 points. He has also earned five club Defender of the Year awards and four Humanitarian of the Year honors. "I just want to thank the fans for supporting me in the good times and the bad times and supporting this club," Farrell said. "You guys are the heartbeat of this. That's why we play. "Still a lot to accomplish this season," he added. "This year's coaching staff has been amazing, even in this transition, this next chapter of my life. It's been an honor to be working alongside and be a part of this team."

item.title: Watch: Real Madrid fans claim to have been kicked out of Camp Nou for celebrating opening goal vs Barcelona
item.description: Watch: Real Madrid fans claim to have been kicked out of Camp Nou for celebrating opening goal vs Barcelona Footage stemming from the Spotify Camp Nou has gone viral in the aftermath of last night’s clash between Barcelona and Real Madrid. This comes as members of the visiting crowd claim to have seen fellow supporters thrown out of the ground, for little more than celebrating their side’s opening goal. Real Madrid are of course fresh off a hugely important triumph in Catalunya’s capital, in the process keeping alive their La Liga title hopes. Kylian Mbappé proved himself match-winner on the night, notching the game’s winner with 87 minutes on the clock after previously opening the scoring during the first-half. Mbappé’s goals sparked chaotic celebrations in the away stand at the Camp Nou, as the travelling fans released all of their frustrations amid a dismal recent streak for their side in El Clásico. And it was in the midst of as much that one group of supporters were left looking dumbfounded. In footage posted to social media in the game’s aftermath, several Real Madrid fans were seen being escorted from their seats out of the stadium. The caption, the accuracy of which remains unclear, simply states: ‘Madridistas get kicked out moments after celebrating Mbappé’s 1st goal’ Conor Laird – GSFN

item.description: The G reen Bay Packers have a short week before taking on the Carolina Panthers on Thursday Night Football on Amazon Prime. Unfortunately, they are going to have to play this Week Eight game with their offensive line even more depleted than it was before. Earlier this year, starting right tackle Zach Tom was lost for the year due to a torn patellar tendon. Aaron Banks, Green Bay’s preferred starting left guard before the season began, has been battling knee and toe injuries and has barely played. Now, the Packers look like they will be without the top two centers on their depth chart for some time. Starting center Sean Rhyan went down early with what is believed to be a high ankle sprain. Just a few plays later, backup center Jacob Monk was taken off the field with a quad injury. Mekhi Becton signed to active roster from practice squad to take his place. — Ryan Wood (@ByRyanWood) October 26, 2026 Monk, a fifth round pick in 2024, has not been the interior force that Green Bay envisioned he would be up to this point in his career. He is being replaced by Mekhi Becton, a veteran offensive lineman who the Packers signed a few weeks ago when Monk and the rest of Green Bay’s offensive line struggled to start the regular season. item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. item.title: Mbappé double secures Real Madrid late victory at Barcelona after Raphinha leveller
item.description: Thirteen years later, José Mourinho led Real Madrid into the Camp Nou as one team and them out again as another having secured the kind of late victory he loves and which opens up a whole new world. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. They had drawn level after Mbappé’s opener, Raphinha scoring, but could not do it again. Continue reading...

The sight of Barcola sprinting back to help his defence and Ronald Araújo smashing into challenges, as Liverpool stubbornly defended their lead and their box in the second half, satisfied Iraola just as much as his side’s incisiveness before the break. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. Nothing erudite, anyway. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
